column4: Those with means are forbidden to let an oath stop them giving to relatives, needy people, and emigrants, and are told to pardon; this directly stages an oath-knot released so provision and forgiveness can resume.
أَقْسَمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ places qasam and aymān together for one emphatic oath, while the collapse of the swearers' deeds exposes the gap between their bound words and action.
God's covenant with Israel joins alms and a goodly loan to the promise لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنكُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمْ; binding commitment, provision, and the covering of wrongs occur in one ayah.

Sincere repentance is promised the covering of wrongs, while the forgiven believers' light runs at their right hands; in the same surah as oath-release, this ayah joins takfīr to the favorable yamin image.
After captives are firmly bound, the command permits gracious release or ransom; the ayah makes loosening a human bond concrete and sets release against its opening image of struck necks.
A husband with no witnesses must give four testimonies by God that he speaks truth, beginning a judicially apportioned oath procedure that recalls the section's qasāma definition.
The accuser's fifth testimony invokes God's curse if he lies, showing the added consequence that seals the repeated sworn speech of 24:6.
The accused wife averts punishment by answering with four testimonies by God that he lies; the oath burden is now redistributed to the opposing party.
Her fifth testimony invokes God's wrath if the husband is truthful, completing the reciprocal judicial oath sequence.

Pilgrims are told to eat from sacrificial animals and feed the destitute poor; immediately before fulfillment of vows in 22:29, provision for the hungry becomes part of carrying a consecrated commitment through.
People once judged by an oath to be beyond God's mercy are commanded to enter the Garden; the outcome explicitly overturns the swearers' verdict.
The deceiver swears to the first pair that he is a sincere adviser, making qasam the vehicle of a harmful lie rather than a binding word repaired by truthful action.
At judgment people are reminded that they had sworn they would never pass away; reality dissolves their confident oath and exposes its false object.
The guilty swear at the Hour that they remained only an hour, so an oath again carries a false claim precisely when moral accounting makes its falsity plain.
تِلْكَ إِذًا قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزَىٰ condemns an inequitable division, supplying the unjust boundary of the section's claim that qasam grows from apportionment.
Following the bans on deceptive oaths, this ayah forbids selling God's covenant for a small price; it contrasts profit from a pledged word with the material cost of repairing one.
A visitation from the Lord circles the garden while its owners sleep, interrupting the oath-bound plan before they can exclude the poor.
By morning the garden has become stripped and dark, so the intended harvest that motivated the oath is itself removed.
The owners conclude that they themselves are deprived; the deprivation they planned for the poor returns upon them.
They glorify their Lord and confess that they were wrongdoers, supplying the penitential verbal response after the wrongful oath and its collapse.

They hope their Lord will replace the garden with something better and turn their desire toward Him; this closes the oath story with repentance and hoped-for replacement, though no material kaffāra is stated.
The command أَوْفُوا۟ بِٱلْعُقُودِ establishes the obligation of fulfilling binding knots at the opening of the same surah that later regulates knotted oaths and their release.

The homicide ruling gives the slain person's brother authority to pardon and receive fair payment, supplying a Quranic legal setting of killing, kin, released claim, and compensation close to the qasāma background.
Mary says she has vowed a fast to the Merciful and therefore will not speak that day; vow, fasting, and restrained utterance meet here, although the fast fulfills rather than expiates the vow.
وَلْيُوفُوا۟ نُذُورَهُمْ commands pilgrims to fulfill their vows immediately after 22:28's feeding of the destitute, creating a specific vow-and-provision sequence.
The she-camel has one water-share and the people another on an appointed day; without using qasam itself, the scene concretely enacts the apportioned share behind the section's division sense.
The hypothetical uttering of fabricated sayings against God supplies a grave false-speech scene shortly after the divine oath formula in 69:38.

The next ayah says the false speaker would be seized باليمين, plausibly by the right hand or by power; either reading gives a boundary case for the section's yamin-as-hand claim, but the lexical sense is interpretively disputed.
If those who swore abstinence resolve on divorce, this ayah states the alternative outcome to return in 2:226, completing that legal oath's required resolution.

The wife of Imran vows what is in her womb as مُحَرَّرًا; the form shares the liberation root with taḥrīr al-raqaba and binds a vow to dedication, although it denotes consecrated service rather than manumission.
